title: Automatic night light
summary: An LED switches on by itself when the room gets dark and off again in daylight.
steps: Place the Nano on the breadboard and connect the LDR module: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, DO to D2.
Connect the LED's long leg to D9 through the 220Ω resistor and its short leg to GND.
Upload the sketch and open Tools → Serial Monitor at 9600 baud.
Cover the LDR with your hand. Turn the blue trimmer until the LED switches on at the darkness you want.
If it works the wrong way round (on in light), change HIGH to LOW in the dark check.
code: // Automatic night light: LED turns on when the room gets dark.
const int LDR_PIN = 2;   // LDR module DO
const int LED_PIN = 9;   // LED through a 220 ohm resistor
// Most LDR modules output HIGH when it is dark.
extensions: Use a bare 12 mm LDR on A0 and fade the LED with analogWrite() instead of on/off.
Add a PIR sensor so the light only comes on when it is dark and someone is there.

title: Obstacle alarm
summary: A buzzer beeps and an LED lights whenever something comes close to the IR sensor.
steps: Wire the IR module to 5V, GND and D2, and the buzzer between D8 and GND.
Upload the sketch.
Move your hand towards the sensor; the onboard LED and the buzzer should react.
Adjust the trimmer on the IR module to set how close an object must be.
code: // Obstacle alarm: beep when something is in front of the IR sensor.
bool objectNear = digitalRead(IR_PIN) == LOW;   // IR module output is active LOW
extensions: Count how many times something passes and print the total.
Mount two IR modules on a robot to avoid walls.

title: Touch lamp
summary: Each tap on the touch pad switches an LED lamp on or off.
steps: Connect the touch module to 5V, GND and D2.
Connect the LED to D9 through the 220Ω resistor.
Upload the sketch and tap the pad: the LED toggles once per tap.
Try sticking the pad behind a thin sheet of plastic; it still works.
code: // Touch lamp: every tap toggles the LED.
if (touched && !wasTouched) {   // act only at the moment of the touch
extensions: Hold the pad to fade the brightness up and down with analogWrite().
Drive a relay module instead of the LED to switch a real lamp.

title: Flame alert
summary: Detects a candle or lighter flame and sounds a pulsing alarm with a flashing red LED.
steps: Wire the flame sensor to 5V, GND and D2; the buzzer to D8; the red LED to D9 through 220Ω.
Upload the sketch and open the Serial Monitor.
Light a candle about 30–50 cm away from the sensor (with an adult nearby).
Turn the trimmer until the alarm triggers reliably but not from room lights.
code: // Flame alert: pulsing alarm when a flame is detected.
if (digitalRead(FLAME_PIN) == LOW) {   // LOW = flame seen on most boards
extensions: Add an MQ2 smoke sensor so the alarm also reacts to smoke.
Turn on a small fan through a relay when a flame is seen.
safety: Only test with a small candle on a non-flammable surface, with an adult present.

title: Rain alarm
summary: Beeps when raindrops land on the rain plate, and powers the sensor only while reading so it lasts longer.
concepts: Powering a sensor from a pin
steps: Connect the rain plate to the small comparator board with the two wires.
Wire the board's VCC to D7 (not 5V), GND to GND and AO to A0. The buzzer goes to D8.
Upload and open the Serial Monitor. Note the reading when the plate is dry.
Sprinkle a few drops of water: the reading falls. Set WET_BELOW between the dry and wet values.
code: // Rain alarm: beep when the plate gets wet.
const int POWER_PIN = 7;    // powers the rain board only while reading
const int WET_BELOW = 500;  // lower reading = more water on the plate
extensions: Show dry / drizzle / heavy rain with three LEDs.
Close a model window with a servo when it starts raining.

title: Double-clap switch
summary: Clap twice to switch a light on, clap twice again to switch it off.
concepts: Counting events in a time window
steps: Wire the sound sensor to 5V, GND and D2, and the LED (or relay IN) to D7.
In a quiet room, turn the sound sensor's trimmer until its LED just goes off.
Upload the sketch and open the Serial Monitor. Clap twice quickly.
If nothing happens, your module may idle LOW: change ACTIVE to HIGH.
code: // Double-clap switch: two claps within 0.8 s toggle the output.
const int OUT_PIN = 7;      // LED or relay module
const int ACTIVE = LOW;     // change to HIGH if your module idles LOW
delay(150);             // ignore the echo of the same clap
// After 0.8 s, decide what the claps meant.
extensions: Use three claps for a second device.
Show the clap count on an LCD.

title: Parking sensor
summary: Beeps faster as an object gets closer, with a steady tone when it is under 10 cm, just like a car.
steps: Wire the HC-SR04: VCC 5V, GND GND, Trig D9, Echo D10. Buzzer on D8.
Upload and open the Serial Monitor to see the distance in cm.
Move a book towards the sensor: beeps speed up below 1 m and become steady below 10 cm.
Point the sensor at hard flat surfaces; soft cloth absorbs the sound.
code: // Parking sensor: faster beeps as you get closer.
long us = pulseIn(ECHO_PIN, HIGH, 30000);   // give up after 30 ms (about 5 m)
extensions: Add green, yellow and red LEDs for far, near and too close.
Show the distance on a 16x2 I2C LCD.

title: Plant thirst indicator
summary: Green, yellow or red LED shows whether your plant's soil is wet, okay or dry.
steps: Push the soil probe into a pot and connect it to the comparator board.
Wire the board's VCC to D7, GND to GND, AO to A0. Connect the three LEDs to D4, D5 and D6.
Upload and open the Serial Monitor. Note readings in dry soil and right after watering.
Adjust the 500 and 750 limits in the code to match your soil.
code: // Plant thirst indicator: green = wet, yellow = okay, red = dry.
int value = analogRead(SOIL_PIN);   // high = dry, low = wet
delay(5000);   // reading less often makes the probe last longer
extensions: Swap in the capacitive soil sensor (SEN-014), which does not corrode.
Chirp a buzzer once an hour when the soil is dry.

title: Door open alarm
summary: Sounds an alarm if a door stays open for more than 3 seconds and reports every open and close.
steps: Connect one reed-switch wire to GND and the other to D2. No resistor is needed thanks to INPUT_PULLUP.
Stick the switch on the door frame and the magnet on the door, about 1 cm apart when closed.
Upload and open the Serial Monitor. Open and close the door.
Change ALARM_AFTER_MS to give yourself more or less time.
code: // Door open alarm: buzz when the door stays open too long.
const unsigned long ALARM_AFTER_MS = 3000;   // 3 s to walk through
bool open = digitalRead(REED_PIN) == HIGH;   // magnet away = switch open = HIGH
extensions: Use it on a fridge door with a 30-second limit.
Count how many times the door opens each day.

title: Serial Plotter thermometer
summary: Reads the LM35 and draws a live temperature graph in the Arduino Serial Plotter, lighting an LED when it is hot.
steps: Hold the LM35 with the flat face towards you: left pin to 5V, middle to A0, right to GND.
Upload the sketch, then open Tools → Serial Plotter at 9600 baud.
Pinch the sensor between your fingers and watch the line rise.
If the LM35 gets hot by itself, power off at once: 5V and GND are swapped.
code: // Serial Plotter thermometer with an over-temperature LED.
for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {   // average 10 readings to reduce noise
return raw * 500.0 / 1023.0;     // 10 mV per degree with a 5 V reference
Serial.println(c, 1);            // Tools > Serial Plotter shows a graph
extensions: Run a fan with PWM that speeds up as it gets warmer.
Use analogReference(INTERNAL) for finer 0.1 °C steps.

title: Weather station
summary: Shows temperature, humidity, air pressure and altitude on a 16x2 LCD using a DHT22 and a BMP280.
steps: Install the three libraries from Tools → Manage Libraries.
Wire the DHT22 to D2. Wire the BMP280 and the LCD to the same I2C pins, A4 (SDA) and A5 (SCL). Power the BMP280 from 3.3V.
If the LCD stays blank, turn the contrast trimmer on its back, or try address 0x3F.
Upload. The LCD shows T/H on line 1 and pressure/altitude on line 2.
Set your local sea-level pressure in readAltitude() for a correct altitude.
code: LiquidCrystal_I2C lcd(0x27, 16, 2);   // try 0x3F if the screen stays blank
float alt = bmp.readAltitude(1013.25);    // set your sea-level pressure
extensions: Predict 'rain likely' when pressure falls more than 3 hPa in 3 hours.
Log readings to a micro SD card every 10 minutes.

title: Automatic plant watering
summary: Waters a plant with a pump when the soil gets dry, stops when it is moist, and refuses to run when the tank is empty.
steps: Calibrate first: upload a sketch that prints analogRead(A0), then note the value in dry air (DRY) and in a glass of water (WET).
Put the water level sensor in the tank and the soil sensor in the pot, keeping its top electronics dry.
Wire the pump through the relay's COM and NO contacts, powered by its own 5V supply (share GND with the Nano).
Enter your DRY and WET values, then upload and watch the Serial Monitor.
Let the soil dry out: the pump runs for up to 10 s, then waits 1 minute for the water to soak in.
code: // Automatic plant watering with tank-empty protection.
const int SOIL_PIN = A0;      // capacitive soil sensor
const int TANK_PIN = A1;      // water level sensor in the tank
const int ALERT_PIN = 13;     // onboard LED: tank empty
const int DRY = 520;          // your reading in dry air
const int WET = 260;          // your reading in a glass of water
const int START_AT = 35;      // % moisture: start watering
const int STOP_AT = 60;       // % moisture: stop watering
const int TANK_MIN = 150;     // below this the tank is empty
const unsigned long MAX_RUN_MS = 10000;   // never pump longer than 10 s
const unsigned long SOAK_MS = 60000;      // wait 1 min for water to soak in
const int RELAY_ON = LOW;     // most relay modules switch on with LOW
digitalWrite(RELAY_PIN, RELAY_OFF);   // set the level before enabling the output
bool soaked = pumpStoppedAt == 0 || millis() - pumpStoppedAt > SOAK_MS;
if (!pumping && moisture < START_AT && tankOk && soaked) pump(true);
if (pumping && (moisture >= STOP_AT || !tankOk || millis() - pumpStartedAt > MAX_RUN_MS)) pump(false);
extensions: Show moisture % and tank state on a 16x2 I2C LCD.
Water only in the morning using a DS3231 real-time clock.
safety: Keep water away from the Nano and the relay. Mount the electronics above the pot.

title: Smart dustbin
summary: The lid opens with a servo when a hand comes near and closes 3 seconds after the hand leaves.
steps: Fix the HC-SR04 on the front of the bin facing outwards.
Mount the servo at the hinge so its arm lifts the lid; tape the arm to the lid.
Wire as shown and upload. Test OPEN_ANGLE and CLOSED_ANGLE for your lid and adjust them.
If the Nano resets when the servo moves, power the servo from a separate 5V supply (shared GND).
code: // Smart dustbin: lid opens when a hand comes near.
if (isOpen && millis() - lastSeen > 3000) {   // close 3 s after the hand leaves
extensions: Add a second ultrasonic sensor inside the lid to show how full the bin is.
Move the lid slowly by stepping the servo angle a few degrees at a time.

title: Gas leak detector with exhaust fan
summary: Watches LPG and smoke levels against a clean-air baseline and starts an exhaust fan with a loud alarm on a leak.
parts: Separate 5V 1A supply for the MQ heaters
steps: Power both MQ sensors from a separate 5V supply. Each heater draws about 150 mA, too much for USB. Connect all grounds together.
Before first use, leave new sensors powered for 24 hours to burn in.
Upload in clean air. The sketch warms up for 60 s and then records the baseline.
Test by releasing a tiny puff of gas from an unlit lighter near the MQ6 (never a flame).
Tune RISE so normal cooking smells don't trigger the alarm.
code: // Gas leak detector: compares readings with a clean-air baseline.
const int LPG_PIN = A0;      // MQ6 AO
const int SMOKE_PIN = A1;    // MQ2 AO
const int RELAY_ON = LOW, RELAY_OFF = HIGH;
const int RISE = 150;        // alarm when a reading rises this much above clean air
lpgBase = average(LPG_PIN);     // clean air becomes the baseline
bool danger = lpg > lpgBase + RISE || smoke > smokeBase + RISE;
extensions: Close a gas valve with a servo when a leak is found.
Send an SMS alert through a SIM800L GSM module.
safety: This is a learning project, not a certified gas alarm. Never test with an open flame, and keep a real gas detector in your kitchen.

title: Digital kitchen scale
summary: Weighs up to 5 kg in grams on an LCD, with a tare button to zero the bowl.
parts: Two flat boards (base and platform) + screws
steps: Screw the load cell between the base board and the platform so it can bend (Z shape). The arrow points down.
Wire the load cell to the HX711, and the HX711, LCD and tare button to the Nano.
Calibrate: set calibration = 1.0, upload, empty the platform, then place a known weight (e.g. a 500 g pack).
Divide the number shown by the real weight in grams. Put that number in calibration and upload again.
Press the tare button with an empty bowl on the scale to zero it.
code: // Digital kitchen scale with tare button.
const int TARE_PIN = 5;           // push button to GND
float calibration = 420.0;        // change this after calibrating (see steps)
float grams = scale.get_units(5);  // average of 5 readings
if (fabs(grams) < 1.0) grams = 0;  // hide tiny drift around zero
extensions: Count identical items (screws, coins) by dividing the total weight by one item's weight.
Add a unit button to switch between g, kg and oz.

title: IR remote switch board
summary: Turns four relays on and off with keys 1–4 on the IR remote, with OK switching everything off.
steps: Install the IRremote library (version 4 or newer).
Wire the receiver to D2 and the relay inputs IN1–IN4 to D4–D7.
Upload, open the Serial Monitor and press each remote key. Note the codes it prints.
If your remote's codes differ, put them in the KEYS array and upload again.
code: // IR remote switch board: keys 1-4 toggle relays, OK switches all off.
const uint8_t KEYS[]   = {0x45, 0x46, 0x47, 0x44};   // keys 1-4 on the kit remote
digitalWrite(RELAYS[i], on ? LOW : HIGH);   // relay modules switch on with LOW
for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) setRelay(i, false);
extensions: Save relay states in EEPROM so they come back after a power cut.
Use the arrow keys to dim an LED strip with PWM.
safety: Practise with low-voltage loads (LEDs, 12V fans). Switching mains through relays needs proper enclosures and an experienced adult.

title: Dual-sensor intruder alarm
summary: Combines a PIR and a microwave radar and only sounds the alarm when both detect movement, cutting false alarms.
steps: Wire the PIR to D2 and the radar to D3. Point both at the same area.
Set the PIR's delay trimmer to the minimum and its jumper to repeat trigger (H).
Upload. Wait 60 s for the PIR to settle; the Serial Monitor says 'Armed'.
Walk in front: the onboard LED shows single triggers, and the buzzer only sounds when both agree.
code: // Dual-sensor intruder alarm: PIR + microwave radar must both trigger.
const unsigned long WINDOW_MS = 2000;   // both must trigger within 2 s
bool pirRecent = pirAt && now - pirAt < WINDOW_MS;
bool radarRecent = radarAt && now - radarAt < WINDOW_MS;
digitalWrite(LED_PIN, pirRecent || radarRecent);   // shows single triggers
extensions: Add a reed switch on the door as a third trigger.
Arm and disarm with a 4-digit code on a touch keypad.

title: Water tank level monitor
summary: A waterproof ultrasonic probe on the tank lid shows the water level in % on an LCD and beeps when nearly full or empty.
steps: Mount the probe in the tank lid pointing straight down, at least 25 cm above the highest water level.
Measure the distance from the probe to the tank bottom (EMPTY_CM) and to the water when full (FULL_CM).
Put both numbers in the sketch and upload.
Keep the Nano and LCD in a weatherproof box. Only the probe goes on the tank.
code: // Water tank level monitor with JSN-SR04T.
const int EMPTY_CM = 120;   // probe to tank bottom
const int FULL_CM = 25;     // probe to water when full (keep >= 25 cm)
delayMicroseconds(20);            // JSN-SR04T likes a longer trigger pulse
long medianCm() {                   // middle of 5 readings ignores odd echoes
if (r[j] < r[i]) { long t = r[i]; r[i] = r[j]; r[j] = t; }
extensions: Switch the water pump motor on at 20% and off at 95% with a relay.
Show litres instead of % using the tank's diameter.

title: Two-sensor line follower
summary: A small robot car follows a black tape track using two TCRT5000 sensors and an L298N motor driver.
steps: Build the chassis. Mount the two sensors at the front, 3–5 mm above the floor and slightly wider apart than the tape.
Wire the sensors to D2/D3 and the L298N as shown. Join the battery GND to the Nano GND.
Hold each sensor over black tape and adjust its trimmer until its LED changes clearly between black and white.
Put the robot on the track with the line between the sensors and switch on.
If it turns the wrong way, swap that motor's two wires on the L298N.
code: const int ON_LINE = HIGH;        // TCRT5000 DO is HIGH over black on most boards
const int ENA = 5, IN1 = 7, IN2 = 8;     // left motor
const int ENB = 6, IN3 = 11, IN4 = 12;   // right motor
void setMotor(int en, int a, int b, int speed) {
int outputs[] = {ENA, IN1, IN2, ENB, IN3, IN4};
delay(2000);                    // time to put the robot on the track
if (!left && !right) drive(SPEED, SPEED);        // line between sensors: straight
else if (left && !right) drive(-TURN, TURN);     // line under left: turn left
else if (!left && right) drive(TURN, -TURN);     // line under right: turn right
else drive(0, 0);                                // both on black: stop
extensions: Upgrade to the 5-sensor array and PID control (see the High-level project).
Add an HC-SR04 so the robot stops for obstacles on the track.

title: Water usage meter
summary: Measures water flow in litres per minute and the total litres used, shown on an LCD with a reset button.
steps: Fit the flow sensor in the pipe with the arrow pointing in the direction of the water flow.
Wire the yellow signal to D2, which is an interrupt pin and catches every pulse.
Upload and run water through: flow (L/min) and total litres appear on the LCD.
Check accuracy by filling a 1 litre bottle; adjust PULSES_PER_LITRE if needed.
code: // Water usage meter with YF-S201 flow sensor.
const int RESET_PIN = 4;                 // push button to GND
const float PULSES_PER_LITRE = 450.0;    // YF-S201: 7.5 Hz per L/min x 60
float litresPerMin = count / 7.5;    // pulses in 1 s = Hz; Hz / 7.5 = L/min
extensions: Close a solenoid valve after exactly 500 ml for a smart dispenser.
Warn about a leak when water flows non-stop for 30 minutes.

title: Finger heart-rate monitor
summary: Detects heartbeats from the light reflected by your fingertip and shows an averaged BPM on an LCD.
parts: Velcro strap or clip to hold the finger
libraries: SparkFun MAX3010x Pulse and Proximity Sensor Library
steps: Install the SparkFun MAX3010x and LiquidCrystal I2C libraries.
Wire the sensor and LCD on the shared I2C pins A4/A5.
Upload, open the Serial Monitor at 115200 baud.
Rest your fingertip on the sensor with light, steady pressure. Keep still for 10 seconds.
Compare the BPM with a phone app or by counting your pulse for 15 s × 4.
code: const byte RATE_SIZE = 4;        // average the last 4 beats
sensor.setPulseAmplitudeRed(0x0A); // dim red LED just shows it is on
for (byte i = 0; i < RATE_SIZE; i++) sum += rates[i];
// Update the LCD only twice a second so no samples are missed.
extensions: Blink an LED and click a buzzer on every beat.
Move to an ESP32 to also calculate SpO2 (the Nano has too little RAM for that algorithm).
safety: For learning only. It is not a medical device and must not be used for health decisions.

title: Smart energy meter
summary: Measures mains voltage, current, real power and kWh used by an appliance, shown on an LCD.
steps: Build everything inside an insulated enclosure. The ZMPT101B input goes across live and neutral; the ACS712 sits in series with the live wire to the socket.
Have an experienced adult check all mains wiring before plugging in.
Upload, plug in a known load such as a 100 W bulb, and measure the voltage with a multimeter.
Adjust V_CAL until Vrms matches the multimeter, then adjust I_CAL until the current matches a clamp meter or the bulb's rating.
Leave it running: the kWh figure grows over time.
code: // Smart energy meter: V, A, W and kWh with EmonLib.
const float V_CAL = 500.0;     // tune until Vrms matches your multimeter
const float I_CAL = 10.0;      // ACS712-20A: 100 mV/A -> start at 10, then tune
if (a < 0.15) { a = 0; w = 0; }       // ignore sensor noise with no load
extensions: Show the cost in ₹ using your electricity tariff per unit.
Save kWh to EEPROM every 10 minutes so it survives power cuts.
safety: DANGER: mains voltage can kill. Do this only with an experienced adult, inside a closed insulated box, and never touch the circuit while it is plugged in.

title: Self-balancing robot
summary: A two-wheeled robot that stays upright by reading its tilt from an MPU6050 and correcting it with a PID loop.
parts: Tall, light chassis (e.g. stacked acrylic plates)
steps: Build a tall chassis with the battery on top. A higher centre of mass makes balancing easier.
Mount the MPU6050 flat and firmly in the middle, with its X axis pointing forward.
Upload with the robot held upright and still. The first second calibrates the gyro.
Tune: set Ki and Kd to 0. Raise Kp until it oscillates, add Kd until it calms, then add a little Ki.
If the motors push the wrong way, swap each motor's wires. Adjust setpoint by 0.5° until it stops drifting.
code: // Self-balancing robot: MPU6050 + complementary filter + PID.

const int ENB = 6, IN3 = 11, IN4 = 12;   // right motor

int outputs[] = {ENA, IN1, IN2, ENB, IN3, IN4};

int out = (int)(Kp * error + Ki * integral + Kd * rate);
extensions: Add wheel encoders so it can hold its position, not just stay upright.
Steer it with an IR remote by nudging the setpoint.

title: Gesture-controlled room
summary: Swipe up or down to switch a lamp, and left or right to open or close a servo window blind, without touching anything.
libraries: SparkFun APDS9960 RGB and Gesture Sensor
steps: Power the APDS9960 from an AMS1117-3.3 module, not the Nano's weak 3V3 pin.
Pass SDA and SCL through the level shifter (LV side 3.3V, HV side 5V).
Upload and open the Serial Monitor. It should print 'Gesture sensor ready'.
Swipe your hand 5–10 cm above the sensor, smoothly and not too fast.
code: // Gesture-controlled room: swipe to control a lamp and a servo blind.
const int LAMP_PIN = 7;     // relay or LED
Serial.println(F("APDS9960 not found. Check 3.3V power and wiring."));
case DIR_UP:    digitalWrite(LAMP_PIN, HIGH); Serial.println(F("UP: lamp on")); break;
case DIR_DOWN:  digitalWrite(LAMP_PIN, LOW);  Serial.println(F("DOWN: lamp off")); break;
case DIR_LEFT:  angle = max(0, angle - 30);   blind.write(angle); Serial.println(F("LEFT")); break;
case DIR_RIGHT: angle = min(180, angle + 30); blind.write(angle); Serial.println(F("RIGHT")); break;
extensions: Use NEAR / FAR gestures to dim the lamp.
Read ambient light from the same chip to open the blind at sunrise.

title: Fingerprint door lock
summary: Unlocks a solenoid lock for enrolled fingerprints, flashes red for unknown ones, and locks out for 30 s after 3 failed tries.
steps: Install the Adafruit Fingerprint library and wire the AS608 (TX → D2, RX → D3).
Open File → Examples → Adafruit Fingerprint → enroll, set the pins to 2 and 3, and enroll your fingers (IDs 1, 2, 3…).
Wire the solenoid lock through the relay's COM/NO contacts with its own 12V supply.
Upload this sketch. Enrolled fingers unlock for 3 s; unknown fingers flash red.
code: // Fingerprint door lock with lockout after 3 failures.
SoftwareSerial fpSerial(2, 3);           // RX <- sensor TX, TX -> sensor RX
const int LOCK_PIN = 7;                  // relay driving the solenoid lock
// Returns the matched ID, -1 for an unknown finger, -2 when no finger is present.
Serial.println(F("Too many tries - locked for 30 s"));
extensions: Log every entry with date and time to an SD card using a DS3231 RTC.
Add a master finger that can enroll new users without a PC.

title: Air quality logger
summary: Records temperature, humidity, gas level and dust density every 10 seconds to a CSV file on a micro SD card.
parts: Micro SD card reader + FAT32 card
steps: Format the SD card as FAT32 and insert it.
Wire the dust sensor's LED circuit with the 150Ω resistor and 220µF capacitor as shown.
Power the board from a 5V 1A supply, because the MQ135 heater needs more than USB comfortably gives.
Upload, let it run for 15 minutes (the MQ135 warms up), then copy AIRLOG.CSV to your PC.
Open the CSV in Excel or Google Sheets and draw a chart of each column.
code: // Air quality logger: DHT22 + MQ135 + GP2Y1010 dust -> SD card CSV.
const int DUST_PIN = A1;       // GP2Y1010 Vo
const int DUST_LED = 7;        // GP2Y1010 LED pin (LOW = LED on)
Serial.println(F("SD card failed - check wiring and FAT32 format"));
extensions: Add a DS3231 RTC so each row has a real date and time.
Turn on an air purifier fan through a relay when dust is high.

title: ECG heart monitor
summary: Plots your heart's electrical signal live in the Serial Plotter and calculates BPM from the R-peaks, with lead-off detection.
steps: Unplug the laptop charger. Run on battery only.
Stick the electrodes: red (RA) on the right chest, yellow (LA) on the left chest, green (RL) on the lower right abdomen.
Upload, then open Tools → Serial Plotter at 115200 baud.
Sit still and breathe normally. You should see a repeating PQRST waveform.
If the line drops to 0, a lead is off: press the electrodes firmly.
code: // ECG heart monitor: 250 Hz sampling, R-peak BPM, lead-off detection.
const unsigned long SAMPLE_US = 4000;   // 250 samples per second
if ((long)(micros() - nextSample) < 0) return;   // wait for the next sample time
// Slowly decaying max/min give a threshold that follows the signal.
if (!aboveThreshold && v > threshold && now - lastPeak > 300) {   // R-peak
extensions: Flash an LED on each R-peak.
Record 30-second clips to an SD card and view them on a PC.
safety: Never connect electrodes while the computer or Nano is powered from a mains charger. This is not a medical device.

title: PID line follower with encoders
summary: A fast line follower that uses five sensors to find the line's exact position, PID steering, and wheel encoders to report speed.
steps: Mount the 5-sensor bar at the front, 5 mm above the floor and centred on the robot.
Fit the 20-slot discs on the motor shafts with the encoders around them.
Upload a quick test that prints each sensor; set ON_LINE to HIGH or LOW to match your board over black.
Start with Kd = 0: raise Kp until it follows smoothly but wobbles, then add Kd to remove the wobble.
